text:
olivia: heads up — p95 on host ingest jumped ~10-15% after last prod deploy. quick triage shows host-side overhead up (tokenize + parse + small writev churn). anyone on it?
raj: yep saw alerts from perf-bot. flame looks like more syscalls in the preparse stage.
mei: i pulled a profile — KV cache hot-hit rate for tiny requests dropped ~8% which increases decode work. suspect batching heuristics + kernel pick for short sequences.
jonathan: instrumented ingress on staging, timestamps: parse_start -> tokenize_start ~1.2ms, tokenize_end -> emit ~5.8ms. big jump compared to baseline (~2.4ms total before).
perf-bot: perf-regression: service=host-ingress metric=p95 latency delta=+12% window=30m link=https://perf/reports/1845555432
olivia: thanks. any indication if grpc vs http path differs?
raj: yes — grpc path is doing a lot of small writev calls; http path coalesces more. writev count per request doubled.
mei: paste of quick perf top snippet (local):
```
# hotspots
preparse_shim_copy        32.1%
http2_writev              21.4%
tokenizer_run             18.5%
kv_cache_lookup           12.0%
other_syscalls            16.0%
```
mei: hypothesis: kernel selection chooses small-batch kernel for sequence len < 64 which trades CPU for smaller mem copies; combined with grpc chunking it's worse.
jonathan: i tried forcing the medium-batch kernel via ENV on a staging host: `REDBATCH_KERNEL=medium` — p95 dropped ~6% but CPU up a bit.
raj: can we tweak batching heuristic to avoid small-batch kernel for mixed small-seq workloads? maybe tune min_batch_timeout or prefer kernel by expected request rate.
olivia: proposal: 1) canary kernel override on a subset of hosts, 2) revert grpc framing to coalesce smaller chunks on host proxy, 3) tweak KV cache admission to avoid thrashing for tiny requests.
mei: i ran a quick A/B locally with `ABATCH_HINT=aggressive` and warmups improved KV hits but initial request latency increased (first-byte moved earlier to preparse).
jonathan: opened PR with conservative heuristic tweak + metrics: https://git.internal/r/redwood/ingress/pull/1234 — changes: min_batch_timeout=80us -> 120us, kernel_pref_order=[medium, small, tiny].
raj: i'll set up routing rule to send 10% of traffic to kernel-pref-canary and watch p95 + writev counts.
deploy-bot: rolling canary started: 10% traffic -> canary-hosts (kernel=medium) at 18:46 UTC
olivia: nice. also add a short-term mitigation to coalesce grpc writes in proxy (reduce writev). jonathan can you own that?
jonathan: yep — will push small proxy change (coalesce window 64->256 bytes) and run staging smoke.
mei: i'll add KV metrics (misses per seq bucket) to the dashboard and set alert threshold if >5% delta.
olivia: timeline: canary 30m, if p95 improves -> roll to 50% and schedule full rollout with rollback plan. if no improvement revert kernel and iterate.
raj: logging note — keep a copy of per-request kernel decision in route debug header so we can trace.
olivia: thanks all — ping when canary results in 30m. :thumbsup:
